items.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01
items.q: Johnny Hodges and I, we worked together.

ctx.x: That's when Barney went with him.

And yeah, Barney Big Odd went with him. And Duke Ellington was looking for me for saxophone, but he couldn't find me. So instead of getting me he got Johnny Hodges. Now Simeon left and he went to Milwaukee and then back he joined Earl Hines band. So Louis Russ, I was around doing anything. I was playing around with different bands, a fellow called Wilkins, a piano player, and Edgar Dow, a piano player, Jinger Young, Richard Cheatham from Cleveland, Ohio. I played a gig with Chick Webb's band. You know, a…
I believe I heard it, Dave Nelson.

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1971-03-13
items.q: We were playing together in Louis Russell's band. We had Johnny Hodges, old saxophone with us you know.

ctx.x: Already did? Yeah. I don't remember. That's fascinating. I was just curious because you have traveled with bands both in the south and in the north and out west.

Well through my life I can see I had an opportunity to play with almost all the great musicians. We were playing together in Louis Russell's band. We had Johnny Hodges, old saxophone with us you know. And I played four years at Disneyland. And we had Johnny Sincere, he's passed. We had the great Monet Moore singing, she's passed. And then we had Louis Armstrong playing with us. He's sick now, he hardly playing anymore. And Johnny Sincere, famous banjo, that was Louis Hot Five, you know. Oh yeah. Johnny Sincere,…
Well something I wanted to ask you, you know, you played so much saxophone with all the big bands, why did you take that clarinet again?
